title: Reading Papers Critically
description: Study identify the research claim, read methods and assumptions, interpret tables and figures, and distinguish evidence from speculation. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Identify the research claim
lessons.description: Write the precise supported claim and the broader claim that remains untested.
lessons.conceptOverview: Separate the paper's central claim from background, implementation details and speculative implications. A useful reading note states what changed, compared with what baseline, and under which conditions.
lessons.whyItMatters: Research claims should match the scope of the evidence.

lessons.title: Read methods and assumptions
lessons.description: List the assumptions required to reproduce and apply the method.
lessons.conceptOverview: Inspect data selection, training conditions and evaluation procedures before interpreting headline results. Hidden assumptions can determine whether a method transfers to another workload.
lessons.whyItMatters: Applicability depends on the method's actual assumptions.

lessons.title: Interpret tables and figures
lessons.description: State both absolute and relative improvement and identify the sample size needed to assess uncertainty.
lessons.conceptOverview: Check metric direction, uncertainty, sample size and comparison conditions. A figure can emphasize relative change while hiding a small absolute difference or a changed baseline.
lessons.whyItMatters: Absolute and relative effects convey different information.

lessons.title: Distinguish evidence from speculation
lessons.description: Design a comparison that isolates the proposed mechanism.
lessons.conceptOverview: Authors may propose explanations that are plausible but not directly tested. Label such explanations as hypotheses and identify experiments that could discriminate between alternatives.
lessons.whyItMatters: Mechanistic explanations need evidence beyond an aggregate gain.
